segments.arabic: [927] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا مالك بن أنس قال: حدثني محمد بن أبي بكر الثقفي قال:
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Malik ibn Anas related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Thaqafi related to me. He said:

segments.arabic: سألت أنسا ونحن غاديان من منى إلى عرفات عن التلبية كيف كنتم تصنعون مع النبي ﷺ قال: كان يلبي الملبي لا ينكر عليه ويكبر المكبر فلا ينكر عليه
segments.english: I asked Anas about the talbiyah while the two of us were going in the morning from Mina to ‘Arafat: ‘What did you use to do with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?’ He said, ‘The one saying the talbiyah would say it without being objected to, and the one saying the takbir would say it without being objected to.’

notes: The complete Abu Nu‘aym → Malik ibn Anas → Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Thaqafi chain remains, including related to me. The selected Anas is not expanded to Anas ibn Malik from Brill or the English comparison.

Both individual reciters and both no-objection clauses remain. The dual morning journey and the general what-did-you-do question are retained; the question is not restricted to how to recite talbiyah as in the EPUB.
Talbiyah and takbir are retained as named utterances without inserting their full formulas into the hadith. Modern printed reference 970; English comparisons Bewley 927 and pinned EPUB 2.15.87.

segments.arabic: [928] حدثنا محمد حدثنا عمر بن حفص قال: حدثنا أبي عن عاصم عن حفصة عن أم عطية قالت
segments.english: Muhammad related to us. ‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us, from ‘Asim, from Hafsah, from Umm ‘Atiyyah. She said:

segments.arabic: كنا نؤمر أن نخرج يوم العيد حتى نخرج البكر من خدرها حتى نخرج الحيض فيكن خلف الناس فيكبرن بتكبيرهم ويدعون بدعائهم يرجون بركة ذلك اليوم وطهرته
segments.english: We used to be commanded to go out on the day of Eid, even bringing the virgin girl out of her secluded room, and even bringing out the menstruating women. They would be behind the people, saying the takbir with their takbir and supplicating with their supplication, hoping for the blessing of that day and its purification.

notes: The selected opening Muhammad and every link through ‘Umar ibn Hafs and his father remain; neither name is expanded from biographical identification.
The two even-bringing-out clauses remain. Behind the people follows الناس; the EPUB’s men and from sins are not inserted. The singular virgin girl and the day’s purification remain as selected.
Modern printed reference 971; English comparisons Bewley 928 and pinned EPUB 2.15.88. No Arabic correction is applied.

segments.arabic: [929] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال: حدثنا عبد الوهاب قال: حدثنا عبيد الله عن نافع عن ابن عمر
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: ‘Ubaydullah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان تركز الحربة قدامه يوم الفطر والنحر ثم يصلي
segments.english: A spear would be planted in front of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Fitr and Sacrifice, then he would pray.

notes: The passive spear-placement wording remains; no person who planted it is identified. The selected text and modern print end then he would pray. Brill adds facing it; that addition is not inserted.
Harbah is rendered spear, distinct from the short spear used for ‘anazah in 930. The EPUB’s sutrah explanation stays outside the translated report.
Modern printed reference 972; English comparisons Bewley 929 and pinned EPUB 2.15.89.

segments.arabic: [930] حدثنا إبراهيم بن المنذر قال: حدثنا الوليد قال: حدثنا أبو عمرو قال: أخبرني نافع عن ابن عمر قال:
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Al-Walid related to us. He said: Abu ‘Amr related to us. He said: Nafi‘ informed me, from Ibn ‘Umar. He said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يغدو إلى المصلى والعنزة بين يديه تحمل وتنصب بالمصلي بين يديه فيصلي إليها
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would go in the morning to the prayer ground. A short spear would be carried before him and set up in front of him at the prayer ground, and he would pray facing it.

notes: The selected Abu ‘Amr and informed me wording remain. Brill expands the name with al-Awza‘i and uses related to me; the selected chain is not harmonized with it.
Carrying, setting up, the prayer-ground location and praying towards the short spear all remain. A sutrah explanation is not imported from the English comparison.
Modern printed reference 973; English comparisons Bewley 930 and pinned EPUB 2.15.90.

segments.arabic: [931] حدثنا عبد الله بن عبد الوهاب قال: حدثنا حماد عن أيوب عن محمد عن أم عطية قالت
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Umm ‘Atiyyah. She said:

segments.arabic: أمرنا أن نخرج العواتق وذوات الخدور
segments.english: We were commanded to bring out the young women and the women in seclusion.

segments.arabic: وعن أيوب عن حفصة بنحوه
segments.english: And from Ayyub, from Hafsah, similarly.

segments.arabic: وزاد في حديث حفصة قال أو قالت
segments.english: He added in Hafsah’s report—he said, or she said:

segments.arabic: العواتق وذوات الخدور ويعتزل الحيض المصلي
segments.english: ‘The young women and the women in seclusion; and the menstruating women should keep apart from the prayer ground.’

notes: The second Ayyub → Hafsah route and the explicit he-said-or-she-said uncertainty remain as separate source spans. Neither English comparison preserves that uncertainty fully.

The selected passive we were commanded is retained without adding the Prophet as its named subject. Brill supplies نبينا and expands Hammad to Hammad ibn Zayd; those words are absent from this selected report.
The two groups are joined by and in both selected clauses. The EPUB’s or in the added clause is not substituted. Modern printed reference 974; English comparisons Bewley 931 and pinned EPUB 2.15.91.

segments.arabic: [932] حدثنا عمرو بن عباس قال: حدثنا عبد الرحمن حدثنا سفيان عن عبد الرحمن قال: سمعت ابن عباس قال
segments.english: ‘Amr ibn ‘Abbas related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman related to us. Sufyan related to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman. He said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas. He said:

segments.arabic: خرجت مع النبي ﷺ يوم فطر أو أضحى فصلى ثم خطب ثم أتى النساء فوعظهن، وذكرهن وأمرهن بالصدقة
segments.english: I went out with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a day of Fitr or Adha. He prayed, then delivered a sermon, then went to the women, admonished them, reminded them and commanded them to give charity.

notes: Both unexpanded ‘Abd al-Rahman names and the I-heard link remain. Brill supplies ibn ‘Abis for the later name; that expansion is not inserted.
The Fitr-or-Adha uncertainty and all three actions towards the women remain. In my boyhood is not added from the EPUB; the chapter heading does not supply new words inside the report.
Modern printed reference 975; English comparisons Bewley 932 and pinned EPUB 2.15.92.

segments.arabic: [933] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا محمد بن طلحة عن زبيد عن الشعبي عن البراء قال
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Talhah related to us, from Zubayd, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’. He said:

segments.arabic: خرج النبي ﷺ يوم أضحى إلى البقيع فصلى ركعتين ثم أقبل علينا بوجهه، وقال إن أول نسكنا في يومنا هذا أن نبدأ بالصلاة ثم نرجع فننحر فمن فعل ذلك فقد وافق سنتنا ومن ذبح قبل ذلك فإنما هو شيء عجله لأهله ليس من النسك في شيء فقام رجل، فقال: يا رسول الله إني ذبحت وعندي جذعة خير من مسنة قال اذبحها ولا تفي عن أحد بعدك
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to al-Baqi‘ on the day of Adha and prayed two rak‘ahs. Then he turned his face towards us and said, ‘The first of our rites on this day of ours is to begin with prayer, then return and sacrifice. Whoever does that has followed our practice. Whoever slaughters before that has merely hastened something for his family; it is no part of the sacrifice.’ A man stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I have slaughtered, and I have a young she-goat better than a mature animal.’ He said, ‘Slaughter it, but it will not suffice for anyone after you.’

notes: The full chain, al-Baqi‘ place name, two rak‘ahs and explicit turning of the face remain. The EPUB’s graveyard identification is not part of the selected text and is not inserted.

The unnamed man remains unnamed. Young she-goat and mature animal follow the provisional lexical treatment already used for جذعة and مسنة; no fixed ages or older sheep are imported from the comparisons.
Modern printed reference 976; English comparisons Bewley 933 and pinned EPUB 2.15.93. The separate Abu Sa‘id chapter quotation is retained outside the report and narration.

segments.arabic: [934] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن سفيان قال: حدثني عبد الرحمن بن عابس قال: سمعت ابن عباس
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abis related to me. He said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas:

segments.arabic: قيل له أشهدت العيد مع النبي ﷺ قال: نعم ولولا مكاني من الصغر ما شهدته حتى أتى العلم الذي عند دار كثير بن الصلت فصلى ثم خطب ثم أتى النساء ومعه بلال فوعظهن، وذكرهن وأمرهن بالصدقة فرأيتهن يهوين بأيديهن يقذفنه في ثوب بلال ثم انطلق هو وبلال إلى بيته
segments.english: He was asked, ‘Did you attend Eid with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?’ He said, ‘Yes. Had it not been for my young age, I would not have attended it. He reached the marker by the house of Kathir ibn al-Salt, prayed, then delivered a sermon. Then he went to the women with Bilal. He admonished them, reminded them and commanded them to give charity. I saw them reaching with their hands and throwing it into Bilal’s garment. Then he and Bilal went to his house.’

notes: The full hearing chain and the passive he-was-asked opening remain. No questioner is identified. The selected from Sufyan is retained; Brill uses a further related-to-us formula.
The age qualification, marker, named house, prayer-before-sermon sequence and final return with Bilal remain. The object thrown into the garment remains it; ornaments is not inserted from the EPUB.
Modern printed reference 977; English comparisons Bewley 934 and pinned EPUB 2.15.94.

segments.arabic: [935] حدثني إسحاق بن إبراهيم بن نصر قال: حدثنا عبد الرزاق قال: حدثنا ابن جريج قال: أخبرني عطاء عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: سمعته يقول
segments.english: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Nasr related to me. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj related to us. He said: ‘Ata’ informed me, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah. He said: I heard him say:

segments.arabic: قام النبي ﷺ يوم الفطر فصلى فبدأ بالصلاة ثم خطب فلما فرغ نزل فأتى النساء فذكرهن وهو يتوكأ على يد بلال وبلال باسط ثوبه يلقي فيه النساء الصدقة
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood on the day of Fitr and prayed. He began with prayer, then delivered a sermon. When he finished, he came down and went to the women and reminded them, leaning on Bilal’s hand. Bilal had spread out his garment, into which the women were throwing charity.

segments.arabic: قلت لعطاء زكاة يوم الفطر قال لا ولكن صدقة يتصدقن حينئذ تلقي فتخها ويلقين قلت: أترى حقا على الإمام ذلك يأتيهن ويذكرهن قال إنه لحق عليهم وما لهم لا يفعلونه
segments.english: I said to ‘Ata’, ‘The zakat of the day of Fitr?’ He said, ‘No, but charity they were giving at that time. A woman would throw in her large rings, and they would throw things in.’ I said, ‘Do you consider that a duty upon the imam—to go to them and remind them?’ He said, ‘It is certainly a duty upon them. Why do they not do it?’

segments.arabic: [936] قال ابن جريج وأخبرني الحسن بن مسلم عن طاوس عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Hasan ibn Muslim also informed me, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. He said:

segments.arabic: شهدت الفطر مع النبي ﷺ وأبي بكر وعمر وعثمان رضى الله تعالى عنهم يصلونها قبل الخطبة ثم يخطب بعد خرج النبي ﷺ كأني أنظر إليه حين يجلس بيده ثم أقبل يشقهم حتى جاء النساء معه بلال، فقال { يا أيها النبي إذا جاءك المؤمنات يبايعنك } الآية، ثم قال حين فرغ منها آنتن على ذلك قالت امرأة واحدة منهن لم يجبه غيرها نعم
segments.english: I attended Fitr with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, ‘Umar and ‘Uthman, may Allah Most High be pleased with them. They would pray it before the sermon, then he would deliver the sermon afterwards. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out. It is as though I am looking at him as he motions with his hand for people to sit. Then he went forward, making his way through them, until he came to the women with Bilal. He said, ‘O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you’—the verse. When he finished it, he said, ‘Are you committed to that?’ One woman among them said, ‘Yes’; no one else answered him.

segments.arabic: لا يدري حسن من هي
segments.english: Hasan did not know who she was.

segments.arabic: قال: فتصدقن فبسط بلال ثوبه، ثم قال هلم لكن فداء أبي وأمي فيلقين الفتخ والخواتيم في ثوب بلال
segments.english: He said, ‘Then give charity.’ Bilal spread out his garment, then said, ‘Come, may my father and mother be ransomed for you.’ They began throwing large rings and rings into Bilal’s garment.

segments.arabic: قال عبد الرزاق الفتخ الخواتيم العظام كانت في الجاهلية
segments.english: ‘Abd al-Razzaq said: The fatakh were the large rings that were used in the time of ignorance.

comparisons.note: The pinned English record combines selected reports 935 and 936. This is part 2 of 2, corresponding to app 936; the two source entries and their chains remain separate.

notes: Ibn Jurayj’s continued chain retains its own opening and links back to 935 without copying that earlier chain into this text. All four honorific expressions remain: two for the Prophet, a dual for Ibn ‘Abbas and a collective after the three named companions.

The shift from they would pray to he would deliver the sermon remains. The hand gesture renders the vocalized causative يجلس in the modern print; Fath al-Bari explicitly notes that vocalization. It is not translated as sitting on his hand.

Only the selected Quran incipit is rendered, followed by the source’s the verse cue; the rest of Quran 60:12 is not invented or inserted. The women’s question, single answer, Hasan’s uncertainty and ‘Abd al-Razzaq’s full lexical explanation remain.

Large rings follows the report’s own fatakh definition. The conjunction with rings remains; no metal or body location is added. The source’s masculine then-he-said after Bilal is retained without supplying an extra speaker name in the English.

segments.arabic: [937] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا أيوب عن حفصة بنت سيرين قالت
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Hafsah bint Sirin. She said:

segments.arabic: كنا نمنع جوارينا أن يخرجن يوم العيد فجاءت امرأة فنزلت قصر بني خلف فأتيتها فحدثت أن زوج أختها غزا مع النبي ﷺ اثنتي عشرة غزوة فكانت أختها معه في ست غزوات فقالت فكنا نقوم على المرضى ونداوي الكلمى فقالت: يا رسول الله على إحدانا بأس إذا لم يكن لها جلباب أن لا تخرج، فقال لتلبسها صاحبتها من جلبابها فليشهدن الخير ودعوة المؤمنين قالت حفصة فلما قدمت أم عطية أتيتها فسألتها أسمعت في كذا وكذا قالت نعم بأبي
segments.english: We used to prevent our girls from going out on the day of Eid. A woman came and stayed at the palace of Banu Khalaf. I went to her, and she related that her sister’s husband had gone on twelve expeditions with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and her sister was with him on six expeditions. She said, ‘We used to tend the sick and treat the wounded.’ She said, ‘Messenger of Allah, is there any blame on one of us if she has no outer garment and does not go out?’ He said, ‘Let her companion cover her with her outer garment, and let them witness the good and the supplication of the believers.’ Hafsah said: When Umm ‘Atiyyah arrived, I went to her and asked her, ‘Did you hear about such-and-such?’ She said, ‘Yes, may my father be ransomed for him.’

segments.arabic: وقلما ذكرت النبي ﷺ إلا قالت بأبي
segments.english: She seldom mentioned the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, without saying, ‘May my father be ransomed for him.’

segments.arabic: قال ليخرج العواتق ذوات الخدور أو قال العواتق وذوات الخدور
segments.english: He said, ‘Let the young women in seclusion go out’—or he said, ‘The young women and the women in seclusion’—

segments.arabic: شك أيوب
segments.english: Ayyub was uncertain.

segments.arabic: والحيض ويعتزل الحيض المصلي وليشهدن الخير ودعوة المؤمنين قالت فقلت لها آلحيض قالت نعم أليس الحائض تشهد عرفات وتشهد كذا وتشهد كذا
segments.english: ‘And the menstruating women. Let the menstruating women keep apart from the prayer ground, and let them witness the good and the supplication of the believers.’ She said: I said to her, ‘The menstruating women?’ She said, ‘Yes. Does not a menstruating woman attend ‘Arafat, and attend such-and-such, and attend such-and-such?’

notes: The full nested account retains the unnamed woman, her sister, the husband’s twelve expeditions, the sister’s six and the two visits by Hafsah. The selected she-said transitions are preserved without replacing them with an inferred named speaker.

Both بأبي expressions are rendered as ransom expressions, consistent with the explicit explanation in ‘Umdat al-Qari, rather than as an oath. The intervening observation retains seldom; it is not changed into always.

Both alternatives about young women, Ayyub’s named uncertainty and the inclusion of menstruating women remain. No place names replace the two final such-and-such placeholders, and the final singular woman remains singular.

Cover her with her outer garment is the existing provisional treatment of the clothing phrase; the English does not decide between disputed practical sharing/lending arrangements. Modern printed reference 980; comparisons Bewley 937 and pinned EPUB 2.15.96.

segments.arabic: [938] حدثنا محمد بن المثنى قال: حدثنا ابن أبي عدي عن ابن عون عن محمد قال: قالت أم عطية
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Ibn Abi ‘Adi related to us, from Ibn ‘Awn, from Muhammad. He said: Umm ‘Atiyyah said:

segments.arabic: أمرنا أن نخرج فنخرج الحيض والعواتق وذوات الخدور
segments.english: We were commanded to go out, so we would bring out the menstruating women, the young women and the women in seclusion.

segments.arabic: قال ابن عون أو العواتق ذوات الخدور
segments.english: Ibn ‘Awn said: Or the young women in seclusion.

segments.arabic: فأما الحيض فيشهدن جماعة المسلمين ودعوتهم ويعتزلن مصلاهم
segments.english: As for the menstruating women, they would witness the gathering of the Muslims and their supplication, but keep apart from their prayer ground.

notes: Ibn ‘Awn’s explicit alternative remains separately attributed. The source conjunction and is not silently removed, and the alternative is not treated as an extra group.

The gathering and supplication are both retained, as is their prayer ground. The selected first plural is bring out, matching the vocalized نخرج in the modern print; no order-giver is named where the Arabic is passive.

segments.arabic: [939] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: حدثنا الليث قال: حدثني كثير بن فرقد عن نافع عن ابن عمر
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us. He said: Kathir ibn Farqad related to me, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان ينحر أو يذبح بالمصلى
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would sacrifice or slaughter at the prayer ground.

notes: The full chain and related-to-me formula remain. Sacrifice or slaughter retains the two selected verbs and their or; it is not changed to and from the chapter heading.
The source does not name an animal, state a festival in this report body or say near the prayer ground. Those details are not imported from chapter context or commentary.

segments.arabic: [940] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا أبو الأحوص قال: حدثنا منصور بن المعتمر عن الشعبي عن البراء بن عازب قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu al-Ahwas related to us. He said: Mansur ibn al-Mu‘tamir related to us, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib. He said:

segments.arabic: خطبنا رسول الله ﷺ يوم النحر بعد الصلاة، فقال من صلى صلاتنا ونسك نسكنا فقد أصاب النسك ومن نسك قبل الصلاة فتلك شاة لحم فقام أبو بردة بن نيار، فقال: يا رسول الله والله لقد نسكت قبل أن أخرج إلى الصلاة وعرفت أن اليوم يوم أكل وشرب فتعجلت وأكلت وأطعمت أهلي وجيراني، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: تلك شاة لحم قال: فإن عندي عناق جذعة هي خير من شاتي لحم فهل تجزي عني قال: نعم ولن تجزي عن أحد بعدك
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed us on the Day of Sacrifice after the prayer. He said, ‘Whoever prays our prayer and performs our sacrifice has fulfilled the sacrifice. Whoever sacrifices before the prayer, that is a sheep for meat.’ Abu Burdah ibn Niyar stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I sacrificed before going out to the prayer. I knew that today was a day of eating and drinking, so I made haste, ate and fed my family and my neighbours.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘That is a sheep for meat.’ He said, ‘I have a young she-goat that is better than two sheep for meat. Will it suffice for me?’ He said, ‘Yes, but it will not suffice for anyone after you.’

notes: The complete chain, both Messenger honorifics, by-Allah oath, before-going-out qualification and both family and neighbours remain. The oath is present in the selected Arabic and both prints but absent from the Bewley comparison.

The selected Ibn Niyar is retained; Bewley’s Ibn Dinar is a comparison difference. The two sheep for meat remain distinct from earlier general sheep wording. No fixed age or explanatory alcohol parenthesis is added.

segments.arabic: [941] حدثنا حامد بن عمر عن حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن محمد أن أنس بن مالك قال
segments.english: Hamid ibn ‘Umar related to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, that Anas ibn Malik said:

segments.arabic: إن رسول الله ﷺ صلى يوم النحر ثم خطب فأمر من ذبح قبل الصلاة أن يعيد ذبحه فقام رجل من الأنصار، فقال: يا رسول الله جيران لي إما قال بهم خصاصة وإما قال: فقر وإني ذبحت قبل الصلاة وعندي عناق لي أحب إلي من شاتي لحم فرخص له فيها
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed on the Day of Sacrifice, then delivered a sermon. He commanded whoever had slaughtered before the prayer to repeat his slaughter. A man of the Ansar stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I have neighbours’—either he said, ‘They are in need,’ or he said, ‘In poverty’—‘and I slaughtered before the prayer. I have a young she-goat dearer to me than two sheep for meat.’ He allowed it for him.

notes: The selected that-Anas-said link is retained without replacing it with Brill’s from-Anas form. Hamid’s transmission is followed by from links, not additional related-to-us formulas.
The two alternative descriptions of the neighbours remain explicit. Dearer to me follows أحب إلي, not the EPUB’s better. The subject is the young she-goat; its flesh is not supplied from Bewley.

segments.arabic: [942] حدثنا مسلم قال: حدثنا شعبة عن الأسود عن جندب قال
segments.english: Muslim related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Aswad, from Jundab. He said:

segments.arabic: صلى النبي ﷺ يوم النحر ثم خطب ثم ذبح، فقال من ذبح قبل أن يصلي فليذبح أخرى مكانها ومن لم يذبح فليذبح باسم الله
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed on the Day of Sacrifice, then delivered a sermon, then slaughtered. He said, ‘Whoever slaughtered before praying must slaughter another in its place. Whoever has not slaughtered must slaughter in the name of Allah.’

notes: The three-step prayer, sermon and slaughter sequence remains, followed by both complete conditional instructions.
The chain’s Muslim and al-Aswad are not expanded from identification outside this selected record. Modern printed reference 985; comparisons Bewley 942 and pinned EPUB 2.15.101.

segments.arabic: [943] حدثنا محمد قال: أخبرنا أبو تميلة يحيى بن واضح عن فليح بن سليمان عن سعيد بن الحارث عن جابر قال:
segments.english: Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu Tumaylah, Yahya ibn Wadih, informed us, from Fulayh ibn Sulayman, from Sa‘id ibn al-Harith, from Jabir. He said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ إذا كان يوم عيد خالف الطريق
segments.english: When it was a day of Eid, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would take a different route.

segments.arabic: تابعه يونس بن محمد عن فليح عن سعيد عن أبي هريرة وحديث جابر أصح
segments.english: Yunus ibn Muhammad corroborated him, from Fulayh, from Sa‘id, from Abu Hurayrah. Jabir’s report is sounder.

notes: The complete opening chain and the full final Yunus → Fulayh → Sa‘id → Abu Hurayrah route remain. The modern print shortens the final route after Fulayh; Brill retains the later links. The selected route is not shortened to match it.

Jabir’s report is sounder is a source transmission assessment, retained separately; it is not a new assessment by the app. The EPUB omits this final route and assessment; Bewley gives an abbreviated corroboration note.
The body’s take-a-different-route wording is retained without adding the outbound/return explanation inside the report. Modern printed reference 986; comparisons Bewley 943 and pinned EPUB 2.15.102.

segments.arabic: [944] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب عن عروة عن عائشة
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

segments.arabic: أن أبا بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه دخل عليها وعندها جاريتان في أيام منى تدففان وتضربان والنبي ﷺ متغش بثوبه فانتهرهما أبو بكر فكشف النبي ﷺ عن وجهه، فقال دعهما يا أبا بكر فإنها أيام عيد
segments.english: Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, came in to her. There were two girls with her during the days of Mina, playing the duff and beating it, while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was covered with his garment. Abu Bakr rebuked them, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, uncovered his face and said, ‘Leave them, Abu Bakr, for these are days of Eid.’

segments.arabic: وتلك الأيام أيام منى
segments.english: Those days were the days of Mina.

segments.arabic: وقالت عائشة رأيت النبي ﷺ يسترني وأنا أنظر إلى الحبشة وهم يلعبون في المسجد فزجرهم عمر، فقال النبي ﷺ دعهم أمنا بني أرفدة
segments.english: ‘A’ishah said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, screening me while I watched the Abyssinians playing in the mosque. ‘Umar rebuked them, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Leave them. You are safe, Banu Arfidah.’

segments.arabic: يعني من الأمن
segments.english: Meaning, in the sense of safety.

notes: Both connected accounts remain one selected entry, with their full common chain. Dar Ibn Kathir numbers them separately as 987 and 988. The app candidate is not split or renumbered; both printed references remain explicit.

The source’s Abu Bakr honorific and four Prophet honorifics remain. Brill adds ‘A’ishah honorifics absent from this input; those are not imported. Girls and Abyssinians follow the selected wording without adding slave status from the English comparisons.

Both drumming verbs remain as playing the duff and beating it. The days-of-Mina explanation and final safety gloss are separate transmission notes and stay in the complete script. The modern print places the first explanation outside the quoted speech too.

Fath al-Bari discusses the selected explicit ‘Umar subject and the wording أمنا. You are safe and the source’s separate safety gloss are retained without inserting a further command to carry on. Comparisons Bewley 944 and pinned EPUB 2.15.103.

segments.arabic: [945] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثني عدي بن ثابت قال: سمعت سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Adi ibn Thabit related to me. He said: I heard Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ خرج يوم الفطر فصلى ركعتين لم يصل قبلها ولا بعدها ومعه بلال
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out on the day of Fitr and prayed two rak‘ahs. He did not pray before it or after it, and Bilal was with him.

notes: The selected related-to-me formula from ‘Adi and I-heard formula from Sa‘id remain. Brill uses informed me at the earlier link; this does not change the selected chain.
Both before-it and after-it clauses, two rak‘ahs and Bilal’s presence remain. The separate Abu al-Mu‘alla chapter report is preserved outside the numbered entry and its narration.
